title: bug: switching approvalMode on the board neither cancels nor arms SPEED auto-approval timers, so a plan armed under SPEED is still auto-approved seconds after the human switches to CONTROL, and plans pending when the human switches to SPEED wait until the next daemon restart
description:
Filed by defect hunt #12 (task-f6f0b580, architect-1dd28c7c). Reproduced at moe/work-2026-10-24 f159784e; the files are unchanged at cbae6070.

PROBLEM (packages/moe-daemon/src/):
- The only settings write path is /ws UPDATE_SETTINGS (server/WebSocketServer.ts:828-833) → StateManager.updateSettings (StateManager.ts:1308) → updateProjectSettings (state/profileRollout.ts:140). That function validates, writes and emits, but never touches the SPEED timers.
- Under SPEED, submit_plan arms a per-task timer (tools/submitPlan.ts armSpeedModeApproval, :114-155).
  - The timer re-checks only that the task is still AWAITING_APPROVAL (:127-128), then writes WORKING with PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED.
  - It never re-reads approvalMode.
- The twin rule: under CONTROL, set_task_status refuses AWAITING_APPROVAL→WORKING ("requires human approval in CONTROL mode", setTaskStatus.ts:151-162). An armed timer bypasses that gate for up to speedModeDelayMs (default 2000 ms) after the human switches to CONTROL.
- The reverse direction: rearmSpeedModeApprovals (submitPlan.ts:170) runs only at startup (index.ts:842).
  - AWAITING_APPROVAL rows that are pending when the human switches CONTROL→SPEED are never armed.
  - They all approve at once after the next daemon restart.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md:190-191 describes SPEED as "auto after delay". Nothing in the docs says a mode switch applies to new submissions only.

EVIDENCE:
- /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/B/zzHuntB_speedModeSwitch.test.ts uses zzHuntB_harness.ts: a real StateManager, McpAdapter and MoeWebSocketServer, a JetBrains-shaped UPDATE_SETTINGS { approvalMode: 'CONTROL', … } and speedModeDelayMs 400. Run in a git-archive snapshot of f159784e: Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2).
  - ✓ twin rule: under CONTROL, set_task_status refuses AWAITING_APPROVAL -> WORKING
  - × a plan armed under SPEED is NOT auto-approved after the board switches the project to CONTROL → AssertionError: expected 'WORKING' to be 'AWAITING_APPROVAL'. A PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED event is logged.
- My re-run: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/me/me-zzHuntB_speedModeSwitch.log
- Plugin reach: the JetBrains MoeSettingsDialog approval-mode combo (MoeCommandSender.kt:80-89, UPDATE_SETTINGS) and the VS Code SettingsPanel (MoeDaemonClient UPDATE_SETTINGS).
- Exposure: this project runs TURBO, which arms no timers. SPEED users are the ones affected.

FIX DIRECTION: after a successful settings write that changes approvalMode:
- becoming CONTROL → call clearAllSpeedModeTimeouts();
- becoming SPEED → call rearmSpeedModeApprovals(state). It is already idempotent: it skips armed rows and non-SPEED projects.
- TURBO can keep armed timers, since it approves anyway.
Both functions are exported from tools/submitPlan.ts. Import them; do not edit submitPlan.ts, which task dd1e00f8 holds. Put the calls in updateProjectSettings (profileRollout.ts) so every settings path gets them. If the state→tools import is unwanted, put them in WebSocketServer.ts's UPDATE_SETTINGS case instead, a hunk distinct from the update_epic row's UPDATE_EPIC case.

FILES: packages/moe-daemon/src/state/profileRollout.ts (or the UPDATE_SETTINGS case of packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts), and a new test such as src/state/approvalModeSwitch.test.ts. docs/CONFIGURATION.md's approvalMode row may gain one sentence. No docs/MCP_SERVER.md change is needed.
definitionOfDone: A plan armed under SPEED is not auto-approved when approvalMode changes to CONTROL before its timer fires: it stays AWAITING_APPROVAL and no PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED event is logged (fake timers or a short speedModeDelayMs).
An AWAITING_APPROVAL row pending when approvalMode changes to SPEED is auto-approved after speedModeDelayMs without a daemon restart, and a row that is already armed is not armed twice.
A new vitest file covers both directions and passes, and the existing submit_plan SPEED-mode tests stay green.
